description: Authored map for scripts/cpo-admission.ts: which pack records each part admits, how each is corrected under the maintainer's decisions of 2026-10-28 and the cross-family check of 2026-10-29/30, and the records, documents, entities and sources added at admission. Records outside both parts' include lists are not admitted.

1.snapshotDescription: Dataset state before part 1 of the compute, power and orbit admission (2026-10-30): the IDs it adds and the rows it changes as they were.
1.scope: On 2026-10-30, by the maintainer’s decisions of 2026-10-28, the first part of a machine-prepared, machine-audited and cross-family-checked candidate pack on compute, power and orbit was admitted: US executive orders and a proclamation on AI infrastructure and its power, Texas S.B. 6, the UK AI Opportunities Action Plan’s recommendation on AI Growth Zones, two Chinese plans on data centres and on AI and energy, US export-control rules and guidance on advanced computing from 2023 to 2026 with their stated links to the AI diffusion rule, Chinese export-control announcements and a suspension, three compute and capital announcements, and a new collection of arguments about compute in orbit: dated passages from 1989 to 2026 that state, contest or bear on eleven propositions about the reasons for and the limits of placing computing in orbit. A legal text states duties, not compliance; an announcement is not a contract, construction or operation; a record says what a text states, not whether an argument is right. All records remain seeds.

2.snapshotDescription: Dataset state before part 2 of the compute, power and orbit admission (2026-10-30): the IDs it adds and the rows it changes as they were.
2.scope: On 2026-10-30, by the maintainer’s decisions of 2026-10-28, the second part of the compute, power and orbit candidate pack was admitted with schema 2.21. Schema 2.21 adds an infrastructure entity’s stated location and operators; what a capacity figure measures and a stated range; dates that parties state as targets, deadlines or terms, kept apart from the dates of records; the predicates announced site, status stated, power agreement, supply agreement, government award, granted equity right, announced plan, launch stated, filed application, regulator decision, accepted for filing and designated zone; letter-of-intent and term-sheet stages, an award stage and the source’s own stage wording; and project and programme spending scopes with their stated basis. The records concern data-centre sites and campuses, capacity and spending plans, power agreements and regulator decisions, chip supply agreements and government awards, and plans, filings and launches of compute in orbit, from 2023 to 2026. An announcement is not a contract, construction or operation; a stated status is the stating party’s account; a target date is a projection; figures are as stated and never summed. All records remain seeds.

Entergy stated on 20 August 2025 that the approval allows it to build three combined-cycle combustion turbine plants tied to Meta’s Richland Parish data centre, two there expected online in late 2028 and one at Waterford by the end of 2029.
cpo-pw-entergy-lpsc-meta-gas.qualification: Dated by the regulator’s own record (cross-family check, item 40): the decision of 20 August 2025, with the written order of 29 August 2025, effective immediately. The cross-family check reads the order as treating the new generation as system resources, not capacity allocated to Meta alone. Plant capacities are not stated in the release, and Entergy’s statement that Meta pays its share of the costs is not a record of the cost terms. The approval also covers transmission and up to 1,500 MW of solar procurement.

newClaims.subject: kolasinski-1989-space-radiation-microcircuits
newClaims.statement: Kolasinski’s paper on the effects of space radiation on electronic microcircuits (NASA/SDIO workshop proceedings, May 1989) states that single-event upsets appear in computer memories as unexplained bit flips, reports upset rates observed in memories in orbit, and describes efforts to harden payload designs and develop devices resistant to single-event effects.

time.note: Publication date of the workshop proceedings in NASA’s Technical Reports Server record (May 1989); no day is printed.

newClaims.qualification: Earliest located among the texts found by the pack’s searches of 2026-10-28 and the cross-family check’s bounded search of 2026-10-29/30, which looked at pre-2024 literature on radiation in space electronics; not a claim that no earlier text exists. The criterion is applied as worded: radiation in orbit disrupts computing hardware (here spacecraft memories and microcircuits), with hardening as the response. The paper concerns spacecraft electronics, not orbital data centres, and argues nothing about placing compute in orbit; the criterion does not require that. It replaces the Lumen Orbit white paper (2024) as earliest located, a correction recorded on the collection page.

newClaims.subject: espi-report-98-2025
newClaims.statement: ESPI Report 98 (November 2025) states that in-orbit servicing remains so costly that deorbiting a failed satellite and launching a replacement is generally considered more cost-effective than sending crews for repairs, and that the maintenance cycle of a space-based data centre is expected to depend heavily on redundancy, which itself increases costs.

time.note: Date of publication on the European Space Policy Institute’s report page; the PDF prints “Published: November 2025”.

newClaims.qualification: Earliest located among the texts found by the pack’s searches of 2026-10-28 and the cross-family check’s bounded search of 2026-10-29/30; not a claim that no earlier text exists. A self-funded policy study; it also reports experts’ suggestion of replacing servers on a five-year cycle by hot-swapping modules, and the development of autonomous repair systems. It replaces the Suncatcher paper (22 November 2025) as earliest located, a correction recorded on the collection page.

newClaims.subject: espi-report-98-2025
